headline: Daily Fundamental View:November 18, 2026

highlights: Aarti Industries surpassed Rs 3,600 Cr in quarterly revenue, driven by fuel additives and Zone 4 commercialisation.
Conversely, Apcotex Industries and NOCIL faced margin pressure from raw material inflation and elevated conversion costs.

Camlin Fine Sciences remained under severe financial stress due to liquidity constraints and continued suspension of its Dahej diphenol facility. • Outlook and Guidance: Sectoral recovery is expected to remain uneven, with high-barrier specialty chemicals, fluorochemicals, and CDMO platforms offering superior earnings visibility.
Commercialisation of recently commissioned capacities is expected to drive operating leverage, while semiconductor chemicals and advanced CDMO platforms remain key growth opportunities.
valuation: Management reaffirmed its FY28 EBITDA target of Rs 1,800–2,200 Cr while maintaining Net Debt/EBITDA below 2.5x. • Apcotex Industries’ performance missed our estimates on all fronts.
Apcotex Industries targets 10–12% volume CAGR over the next 3–5 years, driven by structural demand across automotive and industrial applications.
NOCIL expects FY27 revenue to reach the upper end of its Rs 1,400–1,600 Cr guidance range, with operating EBITDA margins targeted at ~10%.
watch: Adding to market anxiety, reports of a National Security Agency network outage heightened concerns over the resilience of the nation’s technology infrastructure, further weighing on investor sentiment.

Capacity commercialisation emerged as a key operating theme. • Chemistry Plays: Companies leveraging advanced fluorination chemistry, specialty ingredients, and integrated CDMO platforms outperformed.
